title: Small-conductor overcurrent protection limits, NEC 240.4(D)

rule_2023_leadin: Unless specifically permitted in 240.4(E) or (G), the overcurrent protection shall not exceed that required by 240.4(D)(1) through (D)(8) after any correction factors for ambient temperature and number of conductors have been applied.

rows.conditions: (1) Continuous loads do not exceed 5.6 amperes. (2) Overcurrent protection is provided by one of the following: a. Branch-circuit-rated circuit breakers listed and marked for use with 18 AWG copper conductor; b. Branch-circuit-rated fuses listed and marked for use with 18 AWG copper conductor; c. Class CC, Class CF, Class J, or Class T fuses.

notes: Item numbers (D)(1)–(D)(8) are the 2023 numbering (SR-8285 added (D)(3) 14 AWG CCA and renumbered the rest).
The limit applies to the overcurrent device, not the conductor's ampacity: 14 AWG Cu has 20 A in the 75 °C column of Table 310.16 but may not be protected above 15 A.
In the 60 °C column of Table 310.16 the ampacities of 14/12/10 AWG Cu (15/20/30 A) and 12/10 AWG Al (15/25 A) equal these limits.
18 and 16 AWG Cu carry conditions (continuous load limits and listed devices); render the conditions with the value or not at all.
'conductor', not 'wire', in (D)(1)/(D)(2) items a./b. (one 2023-cycle pull; the 2026 draft agrees).

240.4(D)(3) 14 AWG CCA: the Minnesota Board of Electricity minutes of Sept. 22, 2022 (after the 2023 edition was issued) list it: '14 AWG copper-clad aluminum was added to the list of permitted small conductors.' (single pull) and 'Has been added to align with other small conductors permitted per 240.4(D).' (two pulls), so the CCA appeal did not remove (D)(3). Evidence research/sources/round4/R4-8-nfpa-leads.md §2.2.

rule_240_4_b.status: verified-sd2023 (SR-8283; heading, lead-in, condition (3) and closing references; conditions (1)-(2) one 2023-cycle pull equal to two 2026 SD pulls). Condition 3 met for the adjustable-trip provision and conditions (1)-(3) by a post-issuance state-government paraphrase (Minnesota DLI, 2022-09-22). The closing sentence's first word ('If' or 'Where') is still open; don't quote it.
rule_240_4_b.heading: (B) Overcurrent Devices Rated 800 Amperes or Less.
conditions: (1) The conductors being protected are not part of a branch circuit supplying more than one receptacle for cord-and-plug-connected portable loads.

(2) The ampacity of the conductors does not correspond with the standard ampere rating of a fuse or a circuit breaker without overload trip adjustments above its rating (but that shall be permitted to have other trip or rating adjustments).
(3) The next higher standard rating selected does not exceed 800 amperes.
rule_240_4_b.closing_sentence_substance: an adjustable-trip OCPD installed per 240.4(B)(1)-(B)(3) may be set to a value not exceeding the next higher standard value above the conductor ampacity, as shown in Table 240.6(A), where restricted access per 240.6(C) is provided
quote_segments: (B) Overcurrent Devices Rated 800 Amperes or Less.
The next higher standard overcurrent device rating (above the ampacity of the conductors being protected)
shall be permitted to be used, provided all of the following conditions are met:
The conductors being protected are not part of a branch circuit supplying more than one receptacle
The ampacity of the conductors does not correspond with the standard ampere rating of a fuse or a circuit breaker
without overload trip adjustments above its rating
(but that shall be permitted to have other trip or rating adjustments).
The next higher standard rating selected does not exceed 800 amperes.
Where If the overcurrent protective device is an adjustable trip device, installed in accordance with 240.4(B) (1),
(B)(2), and (B)(3), it shall be permitted to be set to a value that does not exceed the next higher standard value
above the ampacity of the conductors being protected as shown in Table 240.6(A)
where restricted access in accordance with 240.6(C) is provided.
rule_240_4_b.condition_3: Met for the substance by the Minnesota Board of Electricity 'NEC 2023 Adoption Review Committee' minutes of Sept. 22, 2022 (tier 3, government paraphrase, retrieved 2026-10-24): 'Requirements of 240.4(B)(1), 240.4(B)(2), and 240.4(B)(3) still apply.' and 'Adjustable trip overcurrent protective device must be provided with restricted access per 240.6(C).' (two pulls on the adjustable-trip lines; canaries '(B)(4)', '240.6(B)' and '65' rejected). The 2022 Standards Council record itself was not seen.
